import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Age distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
ax1.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Age')
ax1.set_ylabel('Count')
ax1.set_title('Age Distribution')
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Income distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
ax2.hist(df['Income'].dropna(), bins=20, color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Income')
ax2.set_ylabel('Count')
ax2.set_title('Income Distribution')
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Education level
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
education_counts = df['Education'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(education_counts.index, education_counts.values, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Education')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
ax3.set_title('Education Level')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 4. Spending by category
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_means = df[spending_cols].mean()
spending_labels = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(spending_labels)))
bars = ax4.bar(spending_labels, spending_means, color=colors, edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax4.set_ylabel('Average Spending')
ax4.set_title('Average Spending by Product Category')
ax4.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 5. Purchase channels
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_totals = df[purchase_cols].sum()
purchase_labels = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store']
ax5.pie(purchase_totals, labels=purchase_labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=['#ff9999','#66b3ff','#99ff99'])
ax5.set_title('Purchase Channel Distribution')

# 6. Income vs Total Spending scatter
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
scatter = ax6.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], alpha=0.6, c=df['Age'], cmap='viridis', s=50)
ax6.set_xlabel('Income')
ax6.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax6.set_title('Income vs Total Spending')
ax6.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax6, label='Age')

# 7. Marital Status
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax7.barh(marital_counts.index, marital_counts.values, color='mediumpurple', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax7.set_xlabel('Count')
ax7.set_title('Marital Status Distribution')
ax7.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# 8. Campaign Response Rate
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
campaign_acceptance = df[campaign_cols].sum()
campaign_labels = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response']
ax8.bar(campaign_labels, campaign_acceptance, color='orange', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_ylabel('Acceptances')
ax8.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Count')
ax8.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax8.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

plt.suptitle('Customer Marketing Campaign Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
